preserved: Modest gabled stone-and-timber bakery with dark slate roof and striped awnings
Central glowing arched bread oven and separate round stone oven
Bread displayed in carts and grouped baskets
Ordinary civilian and militia bread-service queues
River edge, short landing, pines, rough stone and simple fences
reconstruction: Expanded the square source into a deliberately framed landscape rather than cropping it to the old square scene
Reduced crowd density and small ground detail for broad matte-plane readability
Added a modest open account book and grouped bread sizes to support the documented public-accounting arrangement
Named bakery retained as a setting, with anonymous baker role figures rather than an unverified canonical portrait of Marta
limitations: Old bathhouse adaptation appears only as a reused stone ground floor; the legacy source itself depicts a gabled bakery, so its visual identity was preserved instead of inventing a new bathhouse design
No branch-specific price, later gray-wing pastry emblem, timestamp or governance outcome is depicted
The narrow center cover clips most of the left oven arch and loses the separate round oven and queues; it retains glowing bread, the baking frontage, loaf counter, ledger and bread exchange

Marta adapts an abandoned bathhouse for baking; military bread, relief bread and paid bread have public accounts. Different governance choices change supply and access.
Recurring bakery visits show governance through bread size, price and ingredients; the baker records practical effects of each flag.
Planned asset includes refugee hard bread, prosperous gray-wing bread and scarcity price boards, but current topic is one image without stage selector.
